pdf.desc: Local PDFs with contents, full-text search and page translation. Select a passage for an AI summary; notes sit in the margin.

mindmap.title: Mind maps
mindmap.desc: An outline becomes a mind map in a click — edit nodes, icons and link styles. Notes grow into a map you prune as you go.

canvas.desc: Components, connectors and custom node styles for architecture and flowcharts. Select any of it and AI redraws the whole.

image.title: Images & assets

clip.title: Web clipping
clip.desc: A built-in browser with side-by-side tabs: clip an article or an image into Markdown and your library, no extension needed.

focus.title: Focus mode
focus.desc: Only the paragraph you are in stays lit, the rest fades. Native Vim bindings keep your hands on the keyboard.

rhythm.title: Writing rhythm

faq.title: Still have questions?
faq.subtitle: Common questions about desktop licensing, AI setup and local files.

items.q1: What kinds of creators is 大懒猫写作 for?
items.a1: BigLazyCat Writer brings writing, research materials, AI, mind maps and canvas into one desktop workspace for novelists and content creators.
items.q2: Who owns the copyright of AI-generated content?
items.a2: Content generated with 大懒猫写作 and then edited and assembled by you belongs to you. 大懒猫写作 is only a creative assistant and makes no claim over your copyright.
items.q3: Which AI models are supported? Do they cost extra?
items.a3: GLM, DeepSeek, Gemini, OpenAI and other mainstream models are supported out of the box, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works too. Model requests go straight to the provider you configure — no proxying, no revenue share, no markup.
items.q4: Is there only one edition of the desktop app?
items.a4: Yes. The desktop edition has a single tier: one-time purchase, own it forever. No subscription, no free-versus-pro levels — writing, AI, formatting, publishing, canvas and mind maps are all yours after purchase, with future version updates included.
items.q5: Does the 30-day trial need an activation code? What happens when it ends?
items.a5: No activation code needed — download the desktop edition and the 30-day full-feature trial starts right away. After it ends the app becomes read-only while your works and data stay untouched; full features return the moment you buy an activation code.
items.q6: Does the website receive my work?
items.a6: This website provides product information, downloads and documentation. Your desktop files stay on your device. When you use AI, relevant content is sent to the model service you configure.
items.a7: The desktop app supports Windows, macOS and Linux; an Android app is also available. See the official release pages for currently published packages.
items.q8: Can I use my own AI models?
items.a8: Yes. Configure a compatible endpoint, model name and API key in the desktop app, or use locally installed Codex or Claude commands. The help center explains setup.
items.q9: Does the desktop app support plugins? Where do I start building my own?
items.a9: Yes. The desktop app ships a plugin center and a plugin runtime: plugins can provide standalone pages, commands, menu entries, custom file editors and scheduled tasks — the official WeChat publishing and typeset-export features are themselves plugins. Developers should start with the "Plugin development" section in the Help Center, which walks through creating a project from the template, writing the manifest, the SDK surface, and packaging & installation.
